stimuli.text: A block of mass 6 kg on a 30° incline is connected by a light string over a light, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass 7 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.2. The system is released from rest, and the hanging block descends.
A block of mass 1.2 kg on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring. Its position is $$x(t) = 0.14\cos(8t)$$, with x in meters and t in seconds.
Students measure the period of a simple pendulum for several string lengths, using small amplitudes.
A solid sphere (I = ⅖MR²) and a hoop (I = MR²) of equal mass M and radius R are released from rest at the top of the same ramp of height 1.7 m. Both roll without slipping.

questions.stem: A 6 kg cart moving at 5 m/s collides with and sticks to a 8 kg cart at rest. What is their speed after the collision?

options.why: Correct. Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.
Kinetic energy is not conserved here.
Use m₁v₁ for the initial momentum.

questions.explanation: v_f = 6·5/14 = 2.14 m/s; kinetic energy lost = 42.9 J.

questions.stem: A 1.9 kg mass oscillates on a spring with $$k = 110$$ N/m. What is the period?
A motor lifts a 210 kg load 28 m at constant speed in 6 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 3x^2$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 1$$ m to $$x = 2$$ m?

options.why: Integrate; do not just evaluate F.

questions.stem: A planet has 8 times Earth's mass and 4 times Earth's radius. What is the gravitational field strength at its surface? (Earth's is 9.8 N/kg.)
Two springs with constants 40 N/m and 30 N/m are connected in parallel and support a 2 kg mass at rest. How far do they stretch in total?

options.why: Series and parallel rules are reversed.
The force is the weight, mg.

questions.stem: A curve of radius 110 m is banked so that a car at 10 m/s needs no friction. What is the banking angle?

options.why: Measure the angle from the horizontal.
Use tan θ = v²/(rg), from dividing the force components.

questions.stem: A spring with $$k = 170$$ N/m is compressed 0.13 m and launches a 0.2 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: The ½ appears on both sides.

questions.stem: A 0.8 kg ball hits a wall at 13 m/s and rebounds at 4 m/s. The contact lasts 0.02 s. What is the average force from the wall?

options.why: The velocity reverses, so the speeds add.
Correct. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) with the direction reversed.

questions.stem: A boat points straight across a river 70 m wide, moving at 8 m/s relative to the water. The current flows at 6 m/s. How far downstream does the boat land?

options.why: That is a time, not a distance.
Correct. The current does not change the time to cross; it only carries the boat downstream.

questions.stem: An oscillator's position is $$x(t) = 0.08\cos(5t)$$ m. What is its maximum speed?
A particle's position is $$x(t) = 1t^3 + 2t^2 - 4t$$, with x in meters and t in seconds. What is its acceleration at $$t = 3$$ s?

options.why: That is the velocity; differentiate again.
Bring each exponent down as a factor when differentiating.
The derivative of 2bt is 2b, which also remains.

questions.explanation: a(t) = 6t + 4, so at t = 3 the value is 22.

questions.stem: A planet has mass $$7 \times 10^{24}$$ kg and radius $$8 \times 10^{7}$$ m. What is the escape speed from its surface? ($$G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$$ N·m²/kg²)

options.why: That is the circular orbit speed; escape needs √2 times more.

questions.stem: A rod lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 1$$ m and has linear mass density $$\lambda = kx^2$$. Where is its center of mass?

options.why: The exponents are n + 2 and n + 1.

questions.stem: An object's acceleration is $$a(t) = 1t$$ m/s². At $$t = 0$$ it has velocity 2 m/s and is at $$x = 0$$. What is its velocity at $$t = 5$$ s?

options.why: Correct. Integrate a(t) and add the initial velocity.
The acceleration is not constant, so constant-acceleration equations do not apply.

questions.stem: An object of mass 1.9 kg falls from rest with a drag force $$F = -bv$$, where $$b = 0.13$$ kg/s. What is its terminal speed?

options.why: Correct. At terminal speed, mg = bv.
Drag here is linear in v.

questions.explanation: v_T = mg/b = 143 m/s and τ = m/b = 14.6 s.

questions.stem: A constant torque of 16 N·m acts on a wheel ($$I = 0.3$$ kg·m²) initially at rest, through 4 revolutions. What is the wheel's final angular speed?

options.why: Correct. Work τΔθ (in radians) equals ½Iω².

questions.stem: A block slides down a 40° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.15. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?

options.why: Correct. a = g(sin θ − μk cos θ).
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
The component along the incline is mg sin θ.

questions.stem: A wheel spinning at 15 rad/s slows uniformly to rest in 18 s. How many revolutions does it make while stopping?

options.why: Correct. Δθ = ½ω₀t, then divide by 2π.
The average angular speed is ω₀/2.
That is in radians; convert to revolutions.

questions.stem: A car moving at 10 m/s brakes with a constant deceleration of 4 m/s². How far does it travel before stopping?

options.why: Correct. Use v² = v₀² + 2aΔx with v = 0.
That is the stopping time in seconds.

questions.stem: A 62 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating downward at 1 m/s². What does the scale read?

options.why: Correct. The scale reads the normal force: N − mg = ma (up positive).
The acceleration changes the normal force.
Check the direction of the acceleration.

questions.stem: A system obeys $$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -64x$$. What is the period of its motion?

options.why: ω is the square root of the coefficient.

questions.stem: A mass on a spring oscillates with angular frequency 12 rad/s and amplitude 0.14 m. What is its speed when it is 0.112 m from equilibrium?

options.why: That is the maximum speed, at x = 0.
Speed is greatest at equilibrium, not at the ends.
Use A² − x² under a square root.
Correct. v = ω√(A² − x²), from conservation of energy.

questions.stem: A 3 kg ball moving at +7 m/s collides elastically head-on with a 4 kg ball at rest. What is the velocity of the 4 kg ball afterward (positive in the original direction)?

options.why: Correct. Elastic: conserve momentum and kinetic energy (relative velocity reverses).
That would be a sticking collision.

questions.explanation: v₁' = (m₁ − m₂)v/(m₁ + m₂) = -1 m/s; v₂' = 2m₁v/(m₁ + m₂) = 6 m/s.

questions.stem: A uniform 7 m beam weighing 400 N rests on supports at both ends. A 500 N load sits 6 m from the left end. What force does the right support exert?

options.why: That is the left support's force.
Include the beam's weight at its center.
The load is not at the center.
Correct. Take torques about the left support.

questions.stem: A constant torque of 9 N·m acts on a wheel ($$I = 2$$ kg·m²) initially at rest, through 9 revolutions. What is the wheel's final angular speed?

options.why: Correct. Work τΔθ (in radians) equals ½Iω².

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 9 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital speed to A's?
The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 2x^3 - 3x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: Set the derivative, not U, to zero.
Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 6x² − 3 = 0 gives x = 0.707 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 2.5 m is pivoted at one end and released from rest in a horizontal position. What is its angular acceleration just after release?

options.why: Use τ = Iα with I = ML²/3.
Correct. τ = Mg(L/2) and I = ML²/3 give α = 3g/(2L).

questions.stem: A 4 kg block on a horizontal table is connected by a string over a light pulley to a hanging 1 kg block. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the table and the block is 0.2. What is the acceleration of the blocks?

options.why: Include friction on the table block.
Correct. Net force (m₂g − μm₁g) divided by the total mass.

questions.stem: A 5 kg mass hangs from a light string wrapped around a uniform disk pulley of mass 4 kg that turns on a frictionless axle. What is the acceleration of the mass?

options.why: The pulley's inertia reduces the acceleration.
Correct. a = mg/(m + M/2), using I = ½MR² and a = Rα.

questions.explanation: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) give a = 7 m/s².

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 1x^3 - 12x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.
Set the derivative, not U, to zero.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 3x² − 12 = 0 gives x = 2 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 5 m down a 37° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.2. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².

questions.stem: A 1500 kg car heading east at 5 m/s collides with a 1000 kg car heading north at 13 m/s, and they lock together. What is their speed just after the collision?

options.why: Correct. Conserve momentum in x and y separately, then combine.
Momentum is a vector; add components at right angles.
Weight each velocity by its mass.

questions.stem: A 2.5 kg ball on a 0.7 m string moves in a vertical circle. At the bottom of the circle its speed is 4 m/s. What is the tension in the string there?

options.why: Check the direction of gravity relative to the center.
Correct. At the bottom, T − mg = mv²/r.

questions.stem: Point masses of 4 kg and 3 kg are at the ends of a massless rod 4 m long. What is the rotational inertia about the rod's center?

options.why: Each mass is L/2 from the center.
Correct. Sum of mr² with r = L/2.
Measure from the center, not an end.

questions.stem: A 5 kg object at rest experiences a net force $$F(t) = 12t$$ N from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 3$$ s. What is its final speed?

options.why: Correct. Impulse ∫F dt equals the change in momentum.
Divide by the mass to get speed.

questions.explanation: J = ∫F dt = 54 N·s; v = J/m = 10.8 m/s.

questions.stem: A solid sphere rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp of height 3.9 m. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: That is only correct for a hoop.
Correct. mgh = ½mv²(1 + β) with I = ⅖MR².

questions.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 10 m/s at 20° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its maximum height?

options.why: Use the vertical component, v₀ sin θ.
Correct. Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.

questions.explanation: v₀x = 9.4 m/s, v₀y = 3.42 m/s. H = v₀y²/(2g) = 0.597 m.

questions.stem: A 10 g bullet moving at 220 m/s embeds in a 4.6 kg block hanging from strings. How high does the block rise?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.
Find the block's speed after the collision first.
Correct. Momentum for the collision, then energy for the swing.

questions.explanation: V = 0.477 m/s after the collision; h = V²/(2g) = 0.0116 m.

questions.title: Block on an incline with a hanging mass

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a free-body diagram for the 6 kg block, labeling each force.

rubric.criterion: Weight down, normal force perpendicular to the incline, tension up the incline.
Kinetic friction down the incline (opposite the motion).

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the acceleration of the system in terms of the masses, θ, μ and g, then calculate its value.

rubric.criterion: Newton's second law applied to each block (or the system).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the string.
Calculate the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended 1.5 m, and the work done by friction on the incline block during that motion.

rubric.criterion: Work by friction, with a negative sign.

parts.prompt: Sketch (describe) graphs of position, velocity and acceleration versus time for one period, aligned vertically.

rubric.criterion: Position is a cosine starting at +A; velocity is a negative sine starting at 0.
rubric.example: x starts at 0.14 m; v starts at 0 and goes negative.

rubric.criterion: Acceleration starts at its negative maximum and is opposite in sign to position throughout.

parts.prompt: Derive expressions for v(t) and a(t), and determine the maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
Calculate the spring constant and the period.
Calculate the total mechanical energy and describe how kinetic and potential energy vary during one period.

rubric.example: K is maximum at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A; U is the reverse; the sum is constant. Each varies twice per period.

parts.prompt: Describe a procedure the students could use to measure the period accurately, including how to reduce uncertainty.

rubric.example: Time 10 swings with a stopwatch and divide by 10.

rubric.criterion: Keep the amplitude small and repeat trials.
rubric.example: Release from under about 10° and average several trials.

parts.prompt: Identify quantities to graph that would give a straight line, and explain how g can be found from the graph.
Plot (describe) the linearized data and draw a best-fit line. Use it to calculate an experimental value of g.
The students repeat the experiment with a much larger amplitude. Predict how the measured periods would change and explain.

rubric.criterion: Periods increase slightly; the small-angle approximation (sin θ ≈ θ) no longer holds.
rubric.example: The restoring torque is less than proportional to θ at large angles.

parts.prompt: Without calculating, predict which object reaches the bottom first. Justify your prediction using energy.

rubric.example: It has the smaller rotational inertia per MR².

rubric.criterion: Justification: less of its energy goes into rotation, so more is translational kinetic energy.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed at the bottom of an object with rotational inertia βMR², in terms of g, h and β.

rubric.criterion: Energy conservation including both forms of kinetic energy, with v = Rω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of each object at the bottom.
Explain whether your derived expression is consistent with your prediction in part (a), and why neither speed depends on M or R.

rubric.criterion: Smaller β gives larger v, consistent with the prediction.
M and R cancel in the energy equation.
rubric.example: Only the shape factor β matters.
